questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A major characteristic of the monocot root is the presence of:
options: Cambium sandwiched between phloem and xylem along the radius
questions.solution: Vascular cambia are found in dicots and gymnosperms but not in monocots because radial vascular bundle is present in monocot root in which cambium is not present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vascular bundles in monocotyledons are considered closed because:
options: A bundle sheath surrounds each bundle.
There are no vessels with perforations.
Xylem is surrounded all around by phloem.
questions.solution: The vascular bundles of monocotyledonous plants do not contain a layer of meristematic tissue (cambium) as the dicots do. Thus, no new cells can be formed inside the vascular bundles of monocots and their vascular bundles are termed closed whereas those of dicot plants are open.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following endoparasites of humans does show viviparity?
questions.solution: Viviparity means development of an embryo inside the body of mother rather than laying eggs. E.g.: Trichinella spiralis is an endoparasite of human body that shows viviparity whereas the remaining endoparasites lay eggs (oviparity).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following animal is not viviparous?
questions.solution: Platypus is an oviparous mammal i.e. it lays eggs whereas the remaining are viviparous i.e. they give birth to young ones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is mainly responsible for the diversification of insects on land?
questions.solution: Exoskeleton plays a role in defence from the prey and is also an important characteristic in the diversification of many species, e.g., insects having chitin as the form of an exoskeleton.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The guts of cow and buffalo possess:
questions.solution: The Bovine rumen is a niche that has a narrow pH range and is kept fairly stabilized, so that the bacteria in the rumen as well as the intake sacs for food and water are not too disturbed. The organisms responsible for producing methane through bovine rumen are termed methanogens and do so in order to reduce the amount of carbon in the rumen system for fermentation. There are two major divisions within the methanogens found in the bovine rumen. The Methanobrevibacter ruminatium and the Methanosphaera stadtmanae.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
Metacentric chromosomes has centromere in the middle position.
Telocentric chromosomes has centromere at the terminal position.
Submetacentric chromosomes has centromere near the centre but not in the middle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The structures that are formed by stacking of organized flattened membranous sacs in the chloroplasts are:
questions.solution: In the chloroplasts, there are stacks of flattened membranous discs known as thylakoids. They appear as similar stacks of coins. Inside the chloroplast, and they trap the energy from sunlight to carry out photosynthesis. These stacks of thylakoids are known as grana. A system of tubules connects them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes?
questions.solution: Inclusion bodies: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells are stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm, e.g., phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules and glycogen granules. Gas vacuoles are found in blue green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A somatic cell that has just completed the S phase of its cell cycle, as compared to gamete of the same species, has:
options: Twice the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
Same number of chromosomes but twice the amount of DNA
Twice the number of chromosomes and four times the amount of DNA
Four times the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
questions.solution:
S-phase (synthesis phase) is the part of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, but a number of chromosome does not change.

If a cell is diploid then after S phase DNA content in the cell will be 4 C and Chromosome in the cell will be 2 N.

While in a gamete,

DNA content in gamete = C

Chromosome in gamete = N

Hence, the Number of chromosome in a somatic cell will be twice than gamete while DNA content will be four times.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in a biotic community is known as:
questions.solution:
By the definition of stratification, it is the distribution of a community in different levels by various socioeconomic means. The different growth form (trees, shrubs, under shrubs, herbs) determines the structure of a plant community. Stratification is based on mode of arrangement of various growth forms.

In the deep lake, zonation or stratification may be according to the need of light. There are three types of zones differentiated is a deep lake - 

  • Littoral Zone
  • Limnetic zone
  • Profundal zone

The clear stratification (vertical arrangement) in various growths from plants according to the need for light is any dense forest.

Surface dwellers →  Herbs →  under shrubs → Shrubs → Trees

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Secondary succession takes place on/in:
questions.solution: Secondary succession occur where vegetation was present previously, but vegetation was destroyed due to natural or artificial causes i.e. fire, flood, sudden changes in climate landslide. This succession is comparatively more rapid, requires 50-100 years for grassland and 100 – 200 years for forest.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Gross primary productivity is the amount of organic matter produced at given length of time during photosynthesis.

questions.solution: Standing crop represents the total amount or number of living things or of one kind of living thing (such as an uncut farm crop, the fish in a pond, or organisms in an ecosystem) in a particular area at any given time. For example, in a population of deciduous tree between summer and winter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Minerals known to be required in large amounts for plant growth include:
questions.solution:
Major/macroelements/macronutrients/mega nutrients are required in large amounts which include: - C, H, O, N, P, K, Ca, S, Mg, and Fe.
While minor/micronutrients/trace elements are required in very small amounts, these include: - Cu, Zn, Mn, B, Mo, and Cl.
Therefore correct option is (A) which includes only major nutrients/mega elements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Perigynous flowers are found in:
questions.solution: Perigynous flower means thalamus is either disc/cup/flasked shaped. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hilum is a scar on the:
options: Fruit, where it was attached to pedicel
questions.solution:
Hilum is a scar on the surface of a seed marking its point of attachment to the seed stalk (funicle). Seed is developed from ovule and bears many structures that were present on the ovule.

Ovule is considered to be an integumented megasporangium. The ovule consists of the stalk and the body. The stalk is called funicle. One end of the funicle is attached to placenta and the other end to the body of the ovule. The point of attachment of funicle with the body is called hilum. Sometimes funicle gets fused with the body of the ovule one side and forms a ridge known as raphe. The body of the ovule shows two ends: the basal end, often called the chalazal end and the upper end is called micropylar end. The main body of the ovule is covered with one or two envelopes called integuments. These leave an opening at the top of the ovule called micropyle. The integuments enclose a large parenchymatous tissue known as nucellus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What causes a green plant exposed to the light on only one side, to bend toward the source of light as it grows?
options: Green plants need light to perform photosynthesis.
Green plants seek light because they are phototropic.
Light stimulates plant cells on the lighted side to grow faster.
Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating greater cell elongation there.
questions.solution: Auxins accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating grater cell elongation there. Since auxins move from morphological apex to morphological base therefore gets accumulated on the shaded side. Thus plants exposed to the light on only one side bends towards the source of light. It is also due to the tropic movement of auxins which causes phototropism and geotropism in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Typical growth curve in plants is:
questions.solution:
The growth pattern of cells, organisms is uniform under favourable conditions & a typical growth curve in plants is sigmoidal. Thus following phases of growth are recognized.

(i) Lag phase: In the lag period the growth is slow. It represents the formative or cell division phase.

(ii) Log phase: Also called as exponential phase. During this phase, growth is maximum & most rapid. It represents the cell elongation phase.

(iii) Steady or stationary phase: It represents the cell maturation phase.

Time taken in growth phases (mainly log phase) is called a grand period of growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following gametophyte is not independent free living?
questions.solution: In plants (gymnosperms like Pinus and angiosperms), gametophytes is dependent and develop into multicellular organisms while still enclosed within the sporangium while in bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, and hornworts), the gametophyte free living (photosynthetic) e.g. Funaria, Marchantia. In ferns, gametophytes are photosynthetic free living organism called a prothallus (Pteris).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Isogamous reproduction and flagellated gametes can be observed in
questions.solution: Sexual reproduction takes place through the fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following five statements (A to E) and select the option with all correct statements:

(a) Mosses and lichens are the first organisms to colonize bare rock.
(b) Selaginella is a homosporous pteridophyte.
(c) Coralloid roots in Cycas have VAM.
(d) Main plant body in bryophytes is gametophytic, whereas in pteridophytes it is sporophytic.
(e) In gymnosperms, male and female gametophytes are present within sporangia located on sporophytes.
questions.solution:
Mosses are found in moist, shady places, moist rocks, and damp walls or on tree trunks as well as lichens grow on rock surfaces & named by Theophrastus are the first organisms to colonize bare rock.

Selaginella is a heterosporous pteridophye, meaning both male and female spores are produced by the plant.

Coralloid roots of Cycas have nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. Mycorrhiza (VAM) is seen in the roots of Pinus.

Main plant body in bryophytes is gametophyte because gametophyte is dominant over sporophyte as gametophyte is branched, haploid, long-lived and independent whereas sporophyte is diploid short-lived and dependent upon gametophyte. Main plant body in pteridophyte is sporophyte.

Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, the male and the female gametophytes of gymnosperms do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.

Agar-agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria
Chlorella and Spirulina and used a space food
Mannitol is stored food in Rhodophyceae
questions.solution:
Seaweeds contain carrageenan and alginate. Because of their water-holding properties, carrageenan and alginate are extracted from seaweeds and used to thicken a variety of foods, including soy milk, chocolate milk, etc.
Agar or agar-agar, is a jelly-like substance, obtained from red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria. Agar can be used as a laxative, an appetite suppressant, a vegetarian substitute for gelatin, a thickener for soups, etc. 
Chlorella and Spirulina are forms of alga and highly rich in nutrients. They are used as a food supplement by space travellers and athletes.
Mannitol is the stored food in Phaophyceae (brown algae) In Rhodophyceae stored food is floridean starch.

questions.solution:
Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant.

Cross pollination involves the transfer of pollen grains from the flower of one plant to the stigma of the flower of another plant. It is also called xenogamy.

Embryo develops from any diploid cell of embryo sac except egg is referred to as apogamy (diploid apogamy).

Some plants never open to ensure complete self-pollination. This condition is called cleistogamy, e.g., Commelina bengalensis, Oxalis, Viola, etc.

questions.q: Which of the following are the important floral rewards to the animal pollinators?
options: Colour and large size of flower.
questions.solution: The important floral rewards to the animal pollinators are nectar and pollen grain. Plants attract pollinators to their flowers by advertising their floral rewards, i.e., nectar and pollen grain. They take the advantage of the fact that the animals can see, smell and taste by evolving different flower sizes, shapes, colors and scents to selectively attract pollinators.

Pollen grains of some plants cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people
The flowers pollinated by files and bats secrete foul odour to attract them
Honey is made by bees by digesting pollen collected from flowers
questions.solution:

Pollen grains of some plants cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people which may lead to critical medical emergency.

The flowers pollinated by files and bats secrete foul odor which attracts them which, in turn, facilitate the pollination.

Honey is made by bees by digesting the nectar collected from flowers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Transpiration and root pressure cause water to rise in plants by:
questions.solution: In transpiration water rises in plant due to strong cohesive force of transpiration pull in which water is pulled (absorbed) from soil to roots, roots to stem, stem to xylem of leaf and lastly xylem to vein of leaf which is then evaporated. Whereas, root pressure causes passive absorption of water resulting in rise of water in plants i.e. it creates tension in xylem elements which is transmitted downwards up to the root hair, as a result roots are subjected to tension and suction is set up in xylem; hence water is pulled inside the roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a ring girdled plant:
options: The shoot and root die together
Neither root nor shoot will die
questions.solution: In a ring girdled plant the root dies first. Like all vascular plants, trees use two vascular tissues for transportation of water and nutrients: the xylem (also known as the wood), and the phloem (the innermost layer of the bark). Girdling results in the removal of the phloem, and death occurs from the inability of the leaves to transport sugars (primarily sucrose) to the roots. This is an experiment to prove the translocation of food through the phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one gives the most valid and recent explanation for stomatal movements?
questions.solution: The most recent & valid explanation of stomatal movements is given by potassium influx & efflux/potassium ion pump theory which is also as the modern theory. The theory was given by Levitt in 1974. This theory states that the accumulation K+ ions leads to opening of stomata during the day while the reverse situation prevails during dark when the stomata are closed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Because of lanthanoid contraction, which of the following pairs of elements have nearly the same atomic radii? (Number in the parenthesis are atomic numbers).
questions.solution:
Zr 40 and Hf 72: Because of the lanthanoid contraction, Zr (atomic radii 160 pm) and Hf (atomic radii 158 pm) have nearly the same atomic radii.

Lanthanoids include the elements from lanthanum La Z=57 to lutetium Lu Z=71. Zirconium Zr 40 belong to the second transition series 4d and Hf 72 belongs to the third transition series 5d. Lanthanoid contraction is related to the intervention of the 4f-orbitals, which are filled before the 5d-series of elements start. The filling of 4f, if orbitals before 5d-orbitals result in a regular decrease in atomic radii, which compensates the expected increases in atomic size with increasing atomic number. As a result of lanthanoid contraction, the elements of second and third transition series have almost similar atomic radii.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is equal to the second overtone of an organ pipe open at both the ends. The length of the organ pipe open at both the ends is
questions.solution:
For closed organ pipe,
\(n_c=\frac{V}{4 l}\)
For open organ pipe,
\(n_0=\frac{V}{2 l^{\prime}}\)
For the second overtone of an open organ pipe,
\(\begin{aligned}
& n^{\prime}=3 n_0=\frac{3 V}{2 l^{\prime \prime}} \\
& n_c=n^{\prime} \\
& \frac{V}{4 l}=\frac{3 V}{2 l^{\prime}} \\
& l^{\prime}=6 l=6 \times 20 \\
& l^{\prime}=120 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is driven by a machine that delivers a constant power <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> watts. If the particle starts from rest the force on the particle at time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is:
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& F v=\text { constant }=\mathrm{k} \\
& \mathrm{So}, \\
& \frac{\mathrm{mdv}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{v}=\mathrm{k} \\
\Rightarrow & \int \mathrm{vdv}=\int \frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{dt} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{t} \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{t}}
\end{aligned}\)
Now,
\(\begin{aligned}
& F=\frac{\mathrm{mdv}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
& =\mathrm{m} \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}} \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{t}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{mk}}{2}} \mathrm{t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In Bt cotton, the Bt toxin present in plant tissue as pro-toxin is converted into active toxin due to:
options: Alkaline pH of the insect gut
Acidic pH of the insect gut
Presence of conversion factors in insect gut
questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis which contain cry protein in inactive form known as pro-toxin. When this is ingested by insect it get activated by alkaline ph of gut, which solubilize the protein crystal. This activated toxin bind to the epithelial midgut cell result into lysis of epithelial cell and eventually lead to the death of insect.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The crops engineered with Bt-toxin are resistant/tolerant to:
questions.solution: Bt toxin is produced by a bacterium called Bacillus thuringiensis. Bt toxin gene has been cloned from the bacteria and been expressed in plants to provide resistance to insects without the need for insecticides (bio-pesticide). Examples are Bt cotton, Bt corn, rice, tomato, potato and soyabean etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which body of the Government of India regulates GM research and safety of introducing GM organisms for public services?
questions.solution:
Genetic Engineering Approval Committee regulates GM research and safety of introducing GM organisms for public services.

It is also responsible for evaluating numerous activities, including large scale use of microorganisms that are hazardous to the environment. GEAC is also involved in the research and industrial production of the recombinants from the environmental perspective.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Blood pressure in the mammalian aorta is maximum during
questions.solution: Left ventricle drives blood into the aorta during the ventricular systole. Aorta receives blood directly from ventricles and supplies blood to all the body parts. The greater the stroke volume, the greater the change in the aortic pressure. Hence, blood pressure in aorta will be maximum when left ventricle pumps the blood into the aorta.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: Blood is a liquid connective tissue which contains plasma, RBCs, WBCs & Platelet. In animals, it delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When you hold your breath, which of the following gas changes in blood would first lead to the urge to breathe?
questions.solution: The rise in <math><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> concentration stimulates chemoreceptors present in the aorta and carotid artery, which stimulates the respiratory centre. The respiratory centre is not directly sensitive to oxygen concentration & hence desire to breathe is induced by rising in <math><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> the concentration of blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A chemical signal that has both endocrine and neural roles is:
questions.solution:
Epinephrine (also known as adrenaline) is a hormone as well as a neurotransmitter.

Melatonin is involved in blood pressure and autonomic cardiovascular regulation, immune system regulation, and also various physiological functions such as retinal functions, detoxification of free radicals, and antioxidant actions. It also helps in maintaining the balance of circadian rhythms.

Calcitonin (Thyrocalcitonin) acts antagonistically to PTH to reduce calcium levels in the blood.

Cortisol is the main glucocorticoid, helps in maintaining blood glucose level balance as well as maintaining metabolism.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Brunner's glands are present in the submucosa of the stomach and secrete pepsinogen
Goblet cells are present in the mucosa of the intestine and secrete mucus
Oxyntic cells are present in the mucosa of the stomach and secrete HCl
Acini are present in the pancreas and secrete carboxypeptidase
questions.solution: Brunner's glands (or duodenal glands) are compound tubular submucosal glands found in that portion of the duodenum which is above the hepatopancreatic sphincter (Sphincter of Oddi). The main function of these glands is to produce a mucus-rich alkaline secretion (containing bicarbonate), which is the non-enzymatic part of intestinal juice.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gastric juice of infants contains:
questions.solution: Gastric acid is formed in the stomach to aid the process of digestion. In infants, it is released primarily to digest milk protein by rennin, along with small amounts of pepsinogen and lipase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Removal of proximal convoluted tubule from the nephron will result in:
options: No change in quality and quantity of urine
questions.solution: The removal of proximal convoluted tubule from the nephron results in a lack of reabsorption of high threshold substance from renal tubules and obligatory reabsorption of water is also affected leading to more diluted urine. Since proximal convoluted tubules are mainly associated with reabsorption of much water by osmosis, reabsorption of glucose and amino acids by secondary active transport, and other salts and ions as Na+, K+, vitamins etc., by primary active transport.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following does not favor the formation of large quantities of dilute urine?
questions.solution: Renin does not favor for the formation of large quantities of dilute urine as it activates RAAS (Renin-angiotensin activating system), so it causes reabsorption of sodium which leads to the formation of concentrated urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following viruses is not transferred through semen of an infected male?
questions.solution: Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted to humans by infected mosquitoes. Chikungunya virus is spread to people by the bite of an infected mosquito. It causes fever, severe joint pain with other symptoms including headache, muscle pain, joint swelling, or rashes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match each disease with its correct type of vaccine:
 
 (a) Tuberculosis (i) Harmless virus
 (b) Whooping cough (ii) Inactivated toxin
 (c) Diphtheria (iii) Killed bacteria
 (d) Polio (iv) Harmless bacteria
questions.solution:
Tuberculosis - Harmless bacteria - Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Whooping cough - Killed bacteria - Bordetella pertussis

Diptheria - Inactivated toxin - Corynebacterium diphtheriae

Polio - harmless virus - Poliomyelitis virus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The active form of Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite in the
questions.solution: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite in the large intestine of human which causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery). Symptoms of this disease include constipation, abdominal pain, and cramps, stools with excess mucous, and blood clots. The active form of Entamoeba histolytica feeds upon erythrocytes, mucosa, and submucosa of the colon as it causes damage by lysis of epithelial cells, neutrophils, and also red blood cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: HIV that causes AIDS, first starts destroying:
questions.solution: HIV that causes AIDS first starts destroying helper T-lymphocytes which are also called CD4 positive lymphocytes because HIV uses the protein CD4, present on the surface of the cell, to attach itself and try its way into the cell.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Capacitation refers to changes in the:
questions.solution: Sperm capacitation refers to the physiological changes spermatozoa must undergo in order to have the ability to penetrate and fertilize an egg. The changes take place via the sperm cell membrane in which it may be that receptors are made available through the removal of a glycoprotein layer. The area of the acrosomal cap is also so altered thereby that the acrosome reaction becomes possible.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these is not an important component of initiation of parturition in humans?
options: Increase in estrogen and progesterone ratio
questions.solution: Prolactin has no role in parturition, it helps in lactation process, (lactogenic hormone), development of mammary glands (mammotropin) & maintenance of corpus luteum (leutotropin).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cells during gametogenesis is normally diploid?
questions.solution: Spermatogonia or the sperm mother cell is diploid while all other cells are formed as a result of meiotic division and hense are haploid in nature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Hysterectomy is the surgical removal of:
questions.solution:
a) CASTRATION: Castration is surgical removal of testis.

b) HYSTERECTOMY: Removal of the uterus (hystera) is called as hysterectomy.

c) OOPHORECTOMY: Removal of the ovary is called as oophorectomy.

d) VASECTOMY: It is temporary method of sterilization in males. In this method vas deferens are cut and tied both the ends under minor surgical operation.

e) TUBECTOMY: This is a method of female sterilization. It involves surgical removal of a small portion of each fallopian tube. A small incision is made into the lower abdominal cavity and a suture is tied around the fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sliding filament theory can be best explained as:
options: When myofilaments slide pass each other actin filaments shorten while myosin filament do not shorten.
Actin and myosin filaments shorten and slide pass each other.
Actin and myosin filaments do not shorten, rather slide pass each other.
When myofilaments slide pass each other, myosin filaments shorten while actin filaments do not shorten.
questions.solution: In the sliding filament model, the thick and thin filaments past each other, shortening the sarcomere, i.e., actin and myosin filaments do not shorten, rather actin filaments slide over myosin filaments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Glenoid cavity helps in articulation of:
questions.solution: The glenoid cavity (or glenoid fossa of scapula) is a part of the shoulder, located on the lateral angle of the scapula. It is directed laterally and forward and articulates with the head of the humerus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The high value of BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) indicates that:
options: Consumption of inorganic matter in the water is higher by the microbes
questions.solution: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidized by bacteria. The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of oxygen by micro-organisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water. The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In sea urchin DNA, which is double-stranded, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the bases were shown to be cytosine. What are the percentages of other three bases expected to be present in this DNA?
questions.solution:
In the DNA molecule, the nucleotides are base paired according to the Chargaff's rule of base equivalence, and it tells always tells adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.

A = T, G = C

C = 17% So G = 17%

A+G / T+C =1

A + G + C + T = 100

A + 17 + 17 + T = 100

A + T = 100 - 34

So, A = 33%, T = 33% = 66

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gene regulation governing lactose operon of E. coli that involves the lac I gene product is:
options: Positive and inducible because it can be induced by lactose
Negative and inducible because repressor protein prevents transcription
Negative and repressible because repressor protein prevents transcription
Feedback inhibition because excess of <math><mi>β</mi></math> - galactosidase can switch off transcription
questions.solution: In negative regulation, a repressor molecule binds to the operator of an operon and terminates transcription. The lac operon is a negatively controlled inducible operon, where the inducer molecule is allolactose.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A gymnast is able to balance his body upside down even in the total darkness because of:
questions.solution: The vestibular apparatus is present in the inner ear. It is situated above the cochlea. It is made up of three semi-circular canals and otolith organ. The vestibular apparatus is responsible for providing a sense of balance and spatial orientation. This helps in coordinating movement with balance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following regions of the brain is incorrectly paired with its function?
options: Corpus callosum - communication between the left and right cerebral cortices
questions.solution: The cerebellum is involved in the coordination of voluntary motor movement, balance and equilibrium and not language comprehension. It is located just above the brain stem and toward the back of the brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Most animals are tree dwellers in a:
questions.solution: Tropical rain forest shows stratification, where the distribution of plants is more and with many layers. Each layer or storey will be comprised with different fauna. Upper storeys have birds, insects, bats, monkeys, lemurs, tree frogs, lizards and anteaters. Hence, most of the animals are tree dwellers in tropical rain forests.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The following graph depicts changes in two populations (A and B) of herbivores in a grassy field. A possible reason for these changes is that.
options: Both plant populations in this habitat decreased
Population B competed more successfully for food than population A
Population A produced more offspring than population B
Population A consumed the members of population B
questions.solution: Population B competed more successfully for food than population A and hence due to this success was able to increase the number of its offsprings.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The movement of a gene from one linkage group to another is called:
questions.solution: A set of genes at different loci on the same chromosome tend to act as a single pair of genes in meiosis instead of undergoing independent assortment. Chromosome translocation is a chromosome abnormality caused by rearrangement of parts between non-homologous chromosomes. Hence, in translocation there is movement of gene from one linkage group to another and lead to change the position of gene.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How many pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants were studied by Mendel in his experiments?
questions.solution: Mendel had studied 7 pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants in his experiments which are stem height, seed colour, seed shape, pod colour, pod shape, flower position & flower colour.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Multiple alleles are present:
options: At different loci on the same chromosome
At the same locus of the chromosomes
questions.solution: Mendel proposed that each gene has two contrasting forms i.e., alleles, but there are some which are having more than two alternative forms (allele). The presence of more than two alleles for a gene is known as multiple allelism. These alleles are present at the same locus of the chromosomes and can be identified only during population studies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An abnormal human baby with 'XXX' sex chromosomes was born due to:
options: Formation of abnormal sperms in the father
Formation of abnormal ova in the mother
Fusion of two ova and one sperm
Fusion of two sperms and ovum
questions.solution: Formation of abnormal ova i.e., 22 + XX in the mother will lead to birth of baby with 'XXX' genotype, due to chromosomal non disjunction in ova. Nondisjunction is the failure of the chromosomes to disjoin and move to opposite poles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Alleles are:
options: Different molecular forms of a gene
questions.solution:
Allele: Genes which code for a pair of contrasting traits are known as alleles i.e., they are slightly different forms of the same gene.

Heterozygous: An individual having two different alleles(Tt).

Phenotype: It is an observable morphological appearance of an organism.

Homozygous: Two alleles of  a gene are identical (TT or tt).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a sexually transmitted disease?
questions.solution: Encephalitis is an acute inflammation (swelling up) of the brain resulting either from a viral infection or when the body's own immune system mistakenly attacks brain tissue. The most common cause is a viral infection.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: What is the tissue culture technique of micropropagation ?
questions.solution: Micropropagation or PTC (Plant tissue culture) is a technique of producing thousands of plantlets from explant in aseptic environment, it can be performed by callus culture or somatic embryogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Which of the following enhances or induces fusion of protoplasts?
questions.solution: The high molecular weight polymer (1000-6000) of PEG acts as a molecular bridges connecting the protoplasts. Calcium ions linked the negatively charged PEG and membrane surface. When PEG  elute, the surface potential are disturbed, leading to intramembrane contact and  subsequent fusion due to the strong affinity of PEG for water which may cause local dehydration of the membrane and increase fluidity, thus inducing fusion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Erythropoiesis starts in:
questions.solution: Erythropoiesis starts in the liver and spleen in a foetus whereas in adults it starts in the red bone marrow. After birth, erythropoiesis occurs only in the bone marrow.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The terga, sterna and pleura of cockroach body are joined by:
questions.solution: The tough, flexible cuticle between the sclerotized parts (skeletal elements) that allows relative movement is called an arthrodial membrane. The terga, sterna and pleura are chitinous plates which cover the cockroach body. These three are linked together by a thin arthrodial membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In ginger, vegetative propagation occurs through:
questions.solution: Rhizome: It is a thick stem growing horizontally, beneath the soil surface. It has distinct nodes and internodes. The nodes bear small scale leaves with buds in their axils. These buds develop into aerial shoot during favourable conditions. The tip of the rhizome ends in a terminal bud. The lower surfaces of the nodes give out small slender adventitious roots. E.g. ginger, turmeric, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A competitive inhibitor reacts reversibly with the enzyme to form an enzyme-inhibitor complex.
In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor molecule is not chemically changed by the enzyme.
The competitive inhibitor does not affect the rate of breakdown of the enzyme-substrate complex.
The presence of the competitive inhibitor decreases the Km of the enzyme for the substrate.
questions.solution: Competitive inhibition is a form of enzyme inhibition where binding of the inhibitor to the active site on the enzyme prevents binding of the substrate and vice versa. The presence of a competitive inhibitor increases the Km constant of the enzyme (and not decrease), while it does not affect the Vmax. The competitive inhibitor binds at the active site, so decreases the affinity of the enzyme for its substrate, so Km constant increases. If substrate concentration is increased, inhibition overcomes and attains normal Vmax.

questions.q: Which is the most common mechanism of genetic variation in the population of sexually-reproducing organism?

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A population will not exist in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium if:
questions.solution:
The Hardy-Weinberg principle says that allele frequencies in a population are stable and constant from generation to generation as long as

  • The population is large enough and changes in allele frequencies due to chance or accident are insignificant. 
  • Mating occurs at random. 
  • Mutation does not occur or if it does occur it must reach a state of equilibrium. 
  • All the members of the population survive and have equal reproductive rates.

A population will not exist in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium if the individuals mate selectively as the mating has to be random and influences like mutation, natural selection and genetic drift affect the equilibrium.
